The guide · 2026-10-20

10 aviation books to give pilots and aviation enthusiasts

An aviation book can be a better gift than equipment when you know what someone likes to read. This shortlist spans memoir, engineering history, early flight, and the human side of aviation. The order reflects gift suitability across different interests, not a claim that we have reviewed every edition.

By Pilot Gift Guide · From the team behind ATC · How we choose

IN THIS GUIDEHow to chooseThe listRelated guides

How to choose

Check the recipient’s shelves before choosing a familiar title. Use the linked publisher pages to confirm authors, editions, and available formats. These are reading gifts; historical accounts and older technical discussions should not be presented as current flight instruction or substitutes for training.

The list

Our selections prioritize personal relevance, usefulness, and fit for the recipient. Named products and destinations link to official sources where applicable.

  1. 1

    The Wright Brothers — David McCullough

    A starting point for a reader interested in the people behind early flight. Choose this direction when biography appeals more than equipment diagrams.

    Official source: simonandschuster.net ↗
  2. 2

    Fate Is the Hunter — Ernest K. Gann

    A memoir choice for someone drawn to earlier commercial aviation. Check whether the recipient already owns it before buying a frequently mentioned aviation title.

    Official source: simonandschuster.com ↗
  3. 3

    Skunk Works — Ben R. Rich and Leo Janos

    Consider this for an engineering-minded reader interested in aircraft development. It offers a different subject focus from a pilot’s personal flying memoir.

    Official source: hachettebookgroup.com ↗
  4. 4

    West with the Night — Beryl Markham

    A memoir option for someone who enjoys adventure and a strong personal perspective. It can suit a literary reader as well as an aviation enthusiast.

    Official source: us.macmillan.com ↗
  5. 5

    Wind, Sand and Stars — Antoine de Saint-Exupéry

    A choice for a reader interested in reflective writing about aviation and experience. Check the language and translation of the edition you select.

    Official source: penguinrandomhouse.co.za ↗
  6. 6

    The Right Stuff — Tom Wolfe

    Consider this for someone interested in the culture surrounding test flying and early astronauts. Confirm they want the book rather than a film-related gift.

    Official source: academic.macmillan.com ↗
  7. 7

    The Aviators — Winston Groom

    A historical direction for readers interested in Rickenbacker, Doolittle, and Lindbergh. Include the author when searching because other books share the title.

    Official source: penguinrandomhouse.com ↗
  8. 8

    The Spirit of St. Louis — Charles A. Lindbergh

    A first-person account centered on Lindbergh’s transatlantic journey. It suits a specific historical interest rather than a general aircraft-identification need.

    Official source: simonandschuster.com ↗
  9. 9

    A Higher Call — Adam Makos with Larry Alexander

    An option for a reader interested in wartime aviation stories. Check that military history and its subject matter fit their reading preferences.

    Official source: penguinrandomhouse.com ↗
  10. 10

    Stick and Rudder — Wolfgang Langewiesche

    A historically significant discussion of flying for a curious pilot’s bookshelf. Give it as reading material alongside, not instead of, current instruction and official guidance.

    Official source: mheducation.com ↗
These are editorial recommendations and planning ideas, not hands-on test results. Read our selection approach and ATC disclosure.
